intro.title: React.memo
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React app that demonstrates how to use React.memo to prevent unnecessary re-renders of a child component. You will learn the core concept of memoization, which helps optimize performance by caching a component's rendered output and reusing it when props don't change. The main technologies involved are React functional components, props, and the React.memo higher-order component. This beginner-friendly lesson will guide you through implementing React.memo step by step to see its effect on rendering behavior.
intro.usecase: React.memo is essential in performance-critical interfaces where expensive re-renders degrade user experience. You'll use it in dashboard applications with multiple live-updating widgets, where each widget should only re-render when its specific data changes. It's also valuable in e-commerce product filters, where changing one filter shouldn't cause unrelated filter components to re-render. Similarly, in social media feeds with hundreds of post components, React.memo prevents re-rendering posts that haven't changed when new posts are added. This optimization is crucial for maintaining smooth interactions in data-heavy applications.
